candidates.title: Handle Messenger customer messages

demandEvidence.chore: Handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I am building a scenario in Make.com to handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger.

ease.reason: A beginner could mock message classification and a reply draft, but no supplied reference documents messaging or language-model steps.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms handling Messenger inquiries might pay; this build report establishes no external demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock using fictional message text is possible, but image handling, response quality and live integrations are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A draft could be prepared repeatedly, but a person must interpret images and approve every customer response.

evidence.reason: The post identifies customer messages on Messenger as the workflow, but gives no volume, exact output or evidence of unmet external need.

candidates.reason: The post is an author describing a scenario they are building, not a separate unmet request. A fictional message-to-draft experiment is bounded but unsupported by implementation evidence; provisional mean 3.6 is below threshold.

candidates.title: Flag unusual laboratory batch records

demandEvidence.chore: Automate processing of high-frequency batch records generated by laboratory testing instruments.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: laboratory testing instruments generate high-frequency batch records that require automated

ease.reason: A student can test synthetic records and operator-supplied limits, but no supplied reference supports instrument ingestion or validation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: chemical manufacturers might pay for record review support; this Show & Tell gives no buyer or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic prototype can flag simple limit exceptions in four weeks; real instrument formats and validated rules are unavailable.

autonomy.reason: Rule-based flags can repeat, but a qualified person must verify records and make every quality decision.

evidence.reason: The excerpt establishes frequent instrument batch records needing automation, but truncates the task and supplies no detailed rules or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The excerpt states a concrete recurring record-review need, so I assessed a narrow synthetic-data flagging experiment. Its author presents a build rather than an external request, evidence is incomplete, and the provisional mean 3.2 is below threshold.

rejected.title: Founders’ time optimization
rejected.reason: The source says product building and customer acquisition consume increasing founder time, but identifies no specific repeated chore or bounded output. Any proposed task breakdown or automation would invent duties.

rejected.title: Braille-to-piano software quality
rejected.reason: The author says existing software is rarely expressive, but the excerpt gives no concrete input, task to improve, or measurable output. A proposed scoring or music-generation workflow would exceed the evidence.

rejected.title: Browser tab extension
rejected.reason: The assigned excerpt only points to an extension; it provides no concrete task or user request to assess. Its title describes a maker’s product, not a sufficiently specified chore.

rejected.title: Reddit stock chatter analysis
rejected.reason: Only a product title is available. Turning it into stock screening or trading advice would invent a task and introduce unsupported financial claims.

rejected.title: Food-delivery order notifications
rejected.reason: The author is exploring automation for a food-delivery application, but the excerpt does not say which order event, notification recipient, trigger, or result is needed. A useful workflow would require invented requirements.

rejected.title: Business automation and technical fixes
rejected.reason: The author describes a business focus on general automations and small fixes, with no specific customer chore. The attached error-handling documentation is capability evidence only and cannot supply missing demand.

rejected.title: Handle Messenger customer messages
rejected.reason: Assessed as a narrowly proposed fictional message-to-draft experiment; the assigned source is a maker report without validated external need or implementation support, and its provisional mean is below 6.

rejected.title: Flag unusual laboratory batch records
rejected.reason: Assessed using synthetic records and operator-supplied limits; evidence is incomplete and this narrow prototype remains below the 6 threshold.

steps.message: Assessed all eight sealed discussion identities. Two concrete workflows received five provisional ratings but fell below 6; the remaining excerpts lack a sufficiently bounded chore, so no post is proposed.
